## Executive Summary

Mojang's own launcher matters to Omni less as a design source than as the **defining
authority of the public contract** every compliant launcher implements: its metadata
endpoints, file formats, and directory layout ARE the specification, exhaustively documented
by the community (minecraft.wiki) and already consumed by every open-source subject in this
corpus. This black-box study records that contract: the version manifest pipeline
(piston-meta), client.json semantics, the asset-index/objects store, the Java runtime
manifest system, launcher_profiles.json, and the .minecraft layout. Omni consumes these
surfaces identically to Prism/Modrinth/HMCL — through its own meta layer per the
launcher-owned-meta pattern.

As a product, the launcher is a unified multi-title hub (Java, Bedrock for Windows, Dungeons/
Legends historically) distributed via Microsoft Store/MSIX with a bootstrap+launcher split
and bundled per-version Java runtimes. Its feature set is deliberately minimal (profiles,
not instances; no mod management) — the gap that created the entire third-party launcher
market this corpus documents. Auth is the canonical MSA chain; ownership verification
gates play — the EULA baseline Omni holds itself to.

## Architecture Components

### Public metadata pipeline (the contract)

- **Location**: `piston-meta.mojang.com -> client.json -> libraries/assets/java-runtime manifests`
- **Role**: The authoritative version/asset/library/runtime metadata surface all launchers consume
- **Sources**: `wiki-version-manifest`, `wiki-clientjson`

version_manifest_v2.json lists all versions with per-version metadata URLs and sha1s;
client.json declares main class, rule-gated arguments and libraries (OS/arch/feature rules,
natives), the assetIndex reference, download artifacts with hashes, logging config, and the
required javaVersion component; asset indexes map logical names to hashed objects served from
resources.download.minecraft.net; java-runtime manifests describe per-platform bundled JVMs.
Every subject in this corpus implements exactly this pipeline (verified in source in the
prism/modrinth/hmcl dossiers); Omni consumes it through its own normalized meta service per
the corpus-consensus pattern.

### Profile model + .minecraft layout

- **Location**: `.minecraft/ (launcher_profiles.json, versions/, libraries/, assets/, saves/…)`
- **Role**: Shared-directory profiles — the anti-pattern that created the instance-launcher market
- **Sources**: `wiki-launcher-profiles`, `wiki-dotminecraft`

The official launcher runs profiles (version + JVM args + game dir) over one shared
.minecraft by default: mods, saves, and configs collide across profiles unless users manage
game directories manually. The entire MultiMC lineage exists to fix this. Omni's importer
must still read launcher_profiles.json and shared .minecraft layouts to migrate users in —
the largest single migration source by user count.

## Feature Inventory

### instance-model

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Authoritative metadata endpoints | core | 5/5 | adopt | `wiki-version-manifest`, `wiki-clientjson` |
| Profiles over shared directory | core | 1/5 | avoid | `wiki-launcher-profiles`, `wiki-dotminecraft` |

**Authoritative metadata endpoints** — piston-meta version manifests, client.json, asset objects, java-runtime manifests — the spec by existence.

*Omni notes*: Omni consumes these exact surfaces (via its own meta layer). Any format drift here is upstream weather all launchers share; the meta layer is the umbrella.

**Profiles over shared directory** — Profiles share one .minecraft by default; isolation is manual.

*Omni notes*: The founding anti-pattern of this market. Omni is instance-first like the whole third-party corpus.

## Authentication Flows

### Microsoft account login (the canonical chain)

The launcher is the reference implementation of the MSA chain: Microsoft OAuth in Microsoft
surfaces, Xbox/XSTS, Minecraft services token, entitlement + profile gate before play.
Documented publicly; verified against open-source implementations in the prism-launcher
dossier (which records the exact endpoints Omni implements). Ownership verification gating
play is the EULA baseline COMPLIANCE.md holds Omni to.

Steps:

1. Microsoft OAuth (official surfaces) -> 2. XBL/XSTS -> 3. api.minecraftservices.com token ->
4. entitlement + profile verification -> play (see prism-launcher dossier for source-verified
endpoint detail)

*Sources*: `help-launcher`, `eula`

## File Formats

### launcher_profiles.json (json)

- **Path pattern**: `.minecraft/launcher_profiles.json`
- **Sources**: `wiki-launcher-profiles`

Documented profile store: profiles keyed by id (name, type, lastVersionId, gameDir, javaArgs,
icon, timestamps) plus launcher settings. Omni's migration importer reads it to reconstruct
profiles as proper instances.

### client.json (per-version metadata) (json)

- **Path pattern**: `.minecraft/versions/<id>/<id>.json (served from piston-meta)`
- **Sources**: `wiki-clientjson`

The per-version contract: mainClass, arguments (rule-gated), libraries (maven coords,
downloads with sha1/size, OS rules, natives classifiers), assetIndex, downloads
(client/server jars), javaVersion component, logging. The single most load-bearing format in
the entire domain — every loader and launcher in this corpus builds on it.

## Protocols & API Surfaces

### Mojang public metadata + content endpoints

- **Endpoint**: `piston-meta.mojang.com, resources.download.minecraft.net, libraries.minecraft.net, api.minecraftservices.com`
- **Sources**: `wiki-version-manifest`, `wiki-clientjson`, `help-launcher`

The complete public surface: version metadata (piston-meta), hashed asset objects
(resources), library artifacts (libraries), and account/entitlement services
(minecraftservices). All consumption is hash-verified and documented; COMPLIANCE.md §1
requires Omni fetch game content only from these official surfaces.

## Analysis Notes

### ADR-0002 boundary statement

This study uses only public documentation and the community-documented public endpoints that
every launcher (including this corpus's open-source subjects) consumes by design. The
launcher binaries themselves were not inspected. The public contract recorded here is
complete for Omni's purposes: the launcher's proprietary internals are irrelevant when the
entire integration surface is public and better documented than most open standards.

*Sources*: `wiki-clientjson`, `help-launcher`
